description: Our project is VIYAL (வியல்)—an ancient Tamil word meaning "the vast expanse of the cosmos." We are building a clean, lightweight tool to explore NASA datasets ✨
summary:
At 9:46 AM in Colombo, checking if a lunar lander keeps sunlight and Earth radio after a 48-hour launch slip meant opening Moon Trek, LROC QuickMap, and JPL Horizons in separate tabs while my laptop fan screamed like an old prop plane. Someone walked past with tea and asked, "Seri, what can it do?" Four tabs gave zero simple answers.

Viyal (Sangam Tamil for a wide, open expanse) fixes that in one browser tab. Built in Rust/WebAssembly and React/WebGPU, it runs 100% on the user's device with zero backend servers or cloud bills. Pick from 16 landing sites (Artemis III candidates, CLPS, Chandrayaan-3, SLIM, Apollo 11, or custom coordinates), choose a lander, and drag a mast height or 708-hour time slider.

Viyal plots Sun, Earth, and orbital relay paths against LOLA horizon masks with no atmospheric refraction, counts down to sunset and Earthset, compares four sites or dates side by side, runs SQL over 2026 to 2035 windows via DuckDB-Wasm, syncs teams peer to peer over WebRTC, and exports a QR-stamped Flight Readiness PDF. An Educator Mode explains lunar physics for students everywhere.
details:
Live Mission Browser: https://grazeline.web.app

Source Code (Rust/WASM + React/WebGPU): https://github.com/sanjaiyan-dev/viyal-lunar-ops

Full Narrated Walkthrough Video (human voice, Dehiwala accent): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sMIhH768C-VRiHElwBVMDylupTeuHVo7/view

4-Page Technical Dossier PDF: Included in the GitHub repository (Viyal_NASA_SpaceApps_2026_Report.pdf)

Start in the Middle: Why Rahu Is Sitting Inside Line 443 of My Rust Code

Late December 2025 in Dehiwala, Colombo. Cyclone Ditwah had shoved our Sri Lankan A/L exams sideways, vegetable prices had lost their minds, and my father passed away in a government hospital on the morning of December 29. My mother hugged me in the corridor and said two words: "Naan iruken." I am here.

A few days later, she brought two small horoscope notebooks into our hall. I used to mock that stuff my whole life. I walked out ready to roast whoever was visiting. Turns out the visitor was a distant relative working as a medical officer in the UK who admitted he used to fight his own family over horoscopes too. He skipped the superstition and explained Rahu as pure orbital geometry: the exact ascending node where the Moon's 5.14-degree tilted orbit cuts across Earth's ecliptic plane.

Fast forward to this Space Apps weekend. Headphones on, listening to A.R. Rahman and Thiruppugazh hymns (the exact music I used to tease my mom for), debugging why South Pole solar angles drift if you forget the Moon's 18.6-year wobble. And what single line in viyal-core/src/astrodynamics.rs stops the math from drifting?

let omega = (125.0445479 - 1934.1362891 * t + 0.0020754 * t2).rem_euclid(360.0);

That omega variable is the Moon's ascending node. In Tamil almanacs, that point is Rahu. Its 18.6-year precession tilts the Moon relative to the Sun by roughly 1.54242 degrees, deciding whether a ridge near Shackleton Crater stays lit for weeks or freezes to 58 K.

That is Viyal (வியல்), named after the Sangam Tamil word for a wide, open expanse (and highlighted with Sevvai, Tamil for "red-mouthed" Mars). Back in Grade 8, Kotlin coroutines scared me so much I ran to web development just to see pixels move. This weekend, web development dragged me back to Rust systems programming, except the "Hello, World" sits 384,400 km away at the lunar South Pole.

Why Zero Cloud Servers? (The Jaffna Dad Rule)

My dad was a classic Jaffna father. He spent money like water on my physics tuition and books, then scolded me if I left the hall fan and light on for thirty seconds just to walk over and drink water.

Paying monthly US dollar server bills to run orbital trig when every user already has a CPU under their keyboard breaks that rule. And when someone in my house walks past my laptop and asks "Seri, what can it do?", waiting on a slow mobile connection or four agency tabs gives nobody an answer.

So once https://grazeline.web.app loads, everything runs 100% client-side in your browser tab: zero backend servers, zero API fees, and sub-millisecond updates on a budget laptop between physics tuition classes.

What Viyal Does (And How It Answers the Challenge)

Equatorial landings like Apollo 11 are polite: 14 Earth days of overhead Sun, then night. At the lunar South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at 1 to 2 degrees. A crater rim throws a shadow longer than my street, temperatures drop from 392 K to 58 K, and Earth wobbles over a 27.2-day libration cycle behind ridges. Slip a launch by 48 hours and a safe site turns into an abort, as Intuitive Machines' IM-2 Athena showed at Mons Mouton in March 2025.

Viyal turns multi-tab guesswork into one workspace with three tabs:

1. Flight Cockpit

  • 16 Curated Sites + Custom Coordinates: Jump across Artemis III candidates (Mons Mouton, Shackleton Connecting Ridge, Malapert Massif, Nobile Rim 1 & 2, de Gerlache Rim 2, Slater Plain, Haworth, Peak near Cabeus B), ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 (Statio Shiv Shakti), JAXA's SLIM (Shioli Crater), Firefly Blue Ghost M1, Chang'e-6 far-side basin (to see 0% Direct-to-Earth visibility in action), Apollo 11 Tranquility Base, or enter custom lat/lon coordinates.
  • 4 Landers + 0 to 50 m Mast Slider: Switch between CLPS Nova-C, ISRO Vikram/LUPEX, JAXA SLIM, and SpaceX Starship HLS (50 m tower with tighter 5.0 degree high-CG tipping limits and 420 m plume risk). Drag the mast slider and watch terrain shadows clear live.
  • Topocentric Polar Horizon Scope + +48H SCRUB: Plots the 360-degree LOLA horizon mask with a +/- 0.85 degree DEM 1-sigma cone, Sun, Earth, ELFO relay, lunar eclipses, and a ghost Sun showing where light shifts 48 hours later. Vacuum horizon dip (-acos(R / (R + h))) is enforced with zero atmospheric refraction.
  • Countdown KPI Strip: Displays L-Score readiness, Time to Sunset / Sunrise, Time to Earthset / Earthrise, solar power flux (W), and estimated regolith temperature (K).
  • Speyerer 4-Track Synodic Ribbon: Scrub hour by hour across a 708-hour lunar cycle to inspect Power + DTE overlap, cryogenic blackouts, ELFO relay coverage, and Gateway NRHO phasing.
  • 3D Grazing Viewport: Built with Three.js WebGPU and TSL shaders (PBR, THERMAL, SLOPE) with automatic WebGL fallback. Shows Earth's 27.2-day libration loop, sunlit A* rover routes, and lets users Shift+Click to drop a surface comms beacon.
  • Hazard Heatmap + IM-2 Fault Simulator: Runs a 7-tree bagged Random Forest, 5-stage GBDT risk map, epistemic disagreement layer, and ISRO-inspired 3x3 (~48 m) HDA safe-pocket count right inside WASM, plus a toggle to replay IM-2 grazing shadow faults.
  • NASA-STD-3001 AST Compiler: Edit live flight rules (ASSERT slope <= 7.0 DEG;) and compile them in Rust/WASM for instant GO or ABORT checks.
  • Educator Mode: One click swaps technical avionics terms for plain-English explorer stories explaining why polar light, libration, and far-side blackouts work the way they do.

2. Compare Sites & Dates

  • Compare 4 landing sites side by side or 4 launch dates on the same terrain with mini horizon scopes, P10 to P90 sunlit spread, DTE vs relay percentages, a 5-axis science vs engineering radar chart, and an executive pass/fail table.

3. AI & Ephemeris Lab + Team Collaboration

  • DuckDB-Wasm 2026 to 2035 Finder: Runs in-browser SQL across 120 lunar synodic cycles in ~52 ms to rank top illumination and radio windows.
  • NSGA-II Backup Optimizer: When a window hits ABORT, a background Web Worker searches 708 hours for Pareto-optimal 7-day backup windows.
  • JPL Horizons DE441 Validator: Fetches and compares our analytical ephemeris against real NASA/JPL Horizons DE441 / coord@301 / MEAN_ME tables inside DuckDB-Wasm (live proxy in local dev, static calibration bundle on Firebase).
  • Serverless P2P Team Room (Science / Engineering / Educator): Syncs PSR target pins, chat notes, and slider changes live across browsers via Yjs CRDT and Trystero WebRTC over public Nostr relays (plus offline BroadcastChannel).
  • Flight Readiness PDF Export: Exports a one-page A4 FRR dossier using jsPDF with Commonwealth UTC timestamps (DD MMM YYYY), a Tamil வியல் stamp, and a pure-TypeScript ISO/IEC 18004 vector QR code that reopens the exact site, lander, and timestamp when scanned.
  • Flight Director Swarm & WebMCP: Combines millisecond System-1 heuristics, a 6-node LangGraph swarm, navigator.modelContext tool logging, a Human-in-the-Loop approval banner, and optional in-browser WebLLM (SmolLM2-360M on WebGPU) with Quindar radio tones.

Tech Stack & Architecture

  • Rust -> WebAssembly (viyal-core/): wasm-bindgen, serde-wasm-bindgen, smartcore (7-tree RF + 5-stage GBDT trained in WASM memory on 180 stratified samples from NASA PGDA Site04 5 m/px GeoTIFFs), kiddo KD-tree + 8-way sunlit A* traverse planner, custom zero-dependency flight-rule lexer/AST, and Meeus/Cassini astrodynamics.
  • Frontend (viyal/): React 19.3 (with React Compiler and <Activity> tab state preservation), Vite 8, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Three.js WebGPU/TSL, DuckDB-Wasm, Yjs + Trystero WebRTC, @langchain/langgraph, @mlc-ai/web-llm, and jsPDF.

Verification & Honest Engineering Boundaries

We verified our coordinate signs, units, and physics against real benchmarks:

  1. Apollo 11 (20 Jul 1969, 20:17 UTC): Tranquility Base shows ~10.8 degree East grazing Sun.
  2. Chang'e-6 (2 Jun 2024): Apollo Basin on the far side shows 0% DTE line of sight.
  3. IM-2 Athena (6 Mar 2025, 17:31 UTC): Mons Mouton shows ~1.5 degree grazing shadows.
  4. JPL Horizons DE441 (coord@301 / MEAN_ME): Verified in DuckDB-Wasm (Shackleton benchmark residuals within ΔEl -0.00°, ΔAz 0.0° across 14 sample timestamps).

What is real vs approximated:

  • Real / Ground-Truth Basis: Meeus Ch. 25/47/53 + Cassini MOON_ME frame + ΔT + lunar eclipse overlap; stratified slopes and elevations extracted offline from NASA PGDA Site04 5 m/px LOLA GeoTIFFs; and JPL Horizons DE441 validation tables.
  • Approximated / Analytical Models: ESA Moonlight ELFO (24h pass) and Gateway NRHO (156h phasing) use synthetic analytical cadence models rather than full N-body SPICE propagators. Local 64x64 micro-topography around landing sites uses procedural variation around each site's base slope and elevation instead of streaming 400 MB GeoTIFF tiles on mobile connections. Custom user coordinates use a synthesized horizon mask rather than live LOLA tile streaming.

Timeline & Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency

All Viyal application code, Rust WASM modules, UI components, and documentation were created during the November 14 to 15, 2026 hackathon window. Only public space agency data, open-source libraries, and my prior open-source CLI utility urai-ecma (used only as a build/context helper) pre-dated the event.

  • Images: The project cover banner (Viyal_Banner.jpg) was generated with Google Gemini / Nano Banana and is visibly labeled as SI-assisted concept art with zero NASA insignia.
  • Audio: The demo walkthrough video is 100% human-narrated by me in Colombo. Inside the web app itself, the optional Flight Director voice loop uses browser speech synthesis and Web Audio Quindar tones, backed by optional in-browser WebLLM (SmolLM2-360M).
  • Code & Documentation: Gemini and Claude (free tiers, using urai-ecma to fit context limits) helped speed up React/Tailwind scaffolding, three/tsl shader plumbing, and document formatting. No SI was trusted with orbital signs or frame transforms: all Meeus series, Cassini rotations, topocentric parallax, eclipse geometry, and DE441 residuals were derived and checked by hand.

"Even if fate says no, hard work pays its own wage." (Thirukkural 619)
